stories.title: Acylfulvene prodrug LP-184 shows tolerability in glioblastoma trial
stories.summary: Phase 1a data in 16 patients with recurrent glioblastoma established a recommended dose for LP-184, according to Lantern Pharma. The study found the drug well tolerated, though no objective radiographic responses occurred with the single-agent treatment. A combination trial is now planned.

stories.title: Researchers build organ-on-a-chip to study heart cancer resistance
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Toronto have created a multi-organ-on-a-chip device to investigate why the heart is one of the least common sites for cancer metastasis. The platform aims to create new opportunities for cancer research and drug discovery.

stories.title: Inclisiran study shows 46.8 percent LDL cholesterol reduction
stories.summary: A retrospective study of US outpatient clinics found that the therapeutic agent inclisiran reduced LDL cholesterol by a mean of 46.8 percent over twelve months. The data, covering patients treated between 2022 and 2023, showed high rates of treatment adherence among the older population.

stories.title: CRISPR gene editing slashes triglycerides in early trial
stories.summary: A phase 1b trial found that one-time in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 editing of the hepatic ANGPTL3 gene lowered serum triglyceride levels by a mean of 63 percent at 30 days. The findings, presented at the AHA Scientific Sessions, support further study of the one-time treatment strategy.

stories.title: New MRI test aims to color code resistant cancer cells
stories.summary: Scientists are developing an MRI-based test designed to identify treatment-resistant cancer cells. The researchers state the technology could spare some patients from aggressive radiotherapy. The full details of the development are currently available to subscribers.

stories.title: Study finds low relapse risk for rare autoimmune disorder MOGAD
stories.summary: A Kaiser Permanente study published in Neurology reports that patients newly diagnosed with myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease generally experienced a low risk of relapse and lasting disability. The findings offer a positive outlook for those recently diagnosed with the rare condition.

stories.title: Blood pressure medication linked to colitis surgery outcomes
stories.summary: Colitis patients taking a common blood pressure medicine alongside vedolizumab required colon-removal surgery roughly half as often as those who did not. Researchers noted the link was specific to vedolizumab, though medical records cannot prove cause and effect without further randomized trials.

stories.title: High-dose flu vaccine associated with lower Alzheimer's risk
stories.summary: A retrospective cohort study of 164,797 adults aged 65 and older found that those receiving high-dose influenza vaccines had a lower risk of developing Alzheimer's disease than those receiving standard-dose shots. The findings suggest vaccine formulation may influence long-term brain health.

stories.title: CAR-T cell therapy shows early promise for stiff person syndrome
stories.summary: A clinical trial published in JAMA Neurology reports substantial clinical improvement in patients with stiff person syndrome treated with CAR-T cell therapy. Researchers noted that patients rarely return to previous levels of function with existing treatments, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

stories.title: Semaglutide may help reverse chronic kidney disease
stories.summary: Researchers report that semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic, repairs blood vessels and reduces inflammation in kidneys. The study, published in Nature Medicine, suggests the drug can restore kidney function in patients with chronic disease. The drug is finding new uses.

stories.title: COVID-19 vaccine reactions may have nonallergic causes
stories.summary: A randomized trial found that systemic allergic reactions occurred at similar rates in participants receiving vaccines and those receiving a placebo. Laboratory findings suggested that some reported reactions may have nonallergic or nonimmunologic causes, even among patients with histories of severe allergies.

stories.title: Government plans AI-led upgrade for Ayushman Bharat
stories.summary: The Central government plans an AI-led upgrade of the Ayushman Bharat scheme to automate insurance claims and improve fraud detection. The intervention aims to digitize medical records and use data analytics to make healthcare delivery more efficient across the national program.

stories.title: Haryana CM announces subsidised healthcare for low-income families
stories.summary: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini announced that families with an annual income below 5 lakh rupees will receive subsidised treatment at the Shri Sheetla Mata Devi Medical College in Gurugram. The initiative aims to provide needy families with access to affordable healthcare.

stories.title: New AIIMS centers report 6 crore OPD consultations
stories.summary: New AIIMS facilities have recorded over 6 crore outpatient department consultations since the 2021-22 period. The expansion is intended to increase access to specialized tertiary healthcare services across India. The growth reflects a significant increase in patient volume at these institutions.

stories.title: Antibiotics prescribed for nearly half of urban fevers
stories.summary: A prospective study in an urban South Indian community found that 48.55 percent of medically attended fever cases in children and young adults were treated with antibiotics. Broad-spectrum medicines accounted for the majority of these prescriptions, according to findings published in BMC Infectious Diseases.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes immediate license suspension for substandard drugs
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules to allow for the immediate suspension of manufacturing licenses for drugs failing critical quality tests. The move aims to strengthen oversight and prevent the distribution of substandard medicines.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes updates to sterile manufacturing standards
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to Schedule M of the Drugs Rules to align microbial contamination limits with World Health Organization guidelines. The changes seek to strengthen quality control for sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing in India.

stories.title: India hits immunisation milestones
stories.summary: India has eliminated polio and maternal and neonatal tetanus, marking significant public health victories. Despite these achievements, millions of citizens remain unvaccinated. The country continues to run one of the world's largest vaccination drives, though the gap between ambition and total coverage persists in the field.

stories.title: Delhi air quality remains hazardous
stories.summary: Following Diwali, a thick layer of pollution has settled over Delhi. Doctors at AIIMS report that otherwise healthy residents are experiencing respiratory discomfort and persistent coughing. Professor Vijay Hadda warned that the air has become increasingly dangerous, noting that the health consequences now extend beyond vulnerable groups.

stories.title: Former WHO scientist calls for pollution action
stories.summary: Dr. Soumya Swaminathan says India's response to toxic air is too little and too late. Warning that children exposed to high pollution levels may never grow into healthy adults, she advocates for a Covid-like response to manage the country's recurring hazardous air quality and respiratory health crisis.

stories.title: Nepal flood victims may seek climate litigation
stories.summary: Catastrophic floods in Nepal killed thousands in August 2026. Experts suggest exploring climate litigation against major carbon emitters, drawing on legal strategies used in the U.S. and Europe. The full piece on potential legal avenues for these victims is available for subscribers.

stories.title: Palnadu leads in public health satisfaction
stories.summary: Palnadu district topped Andhra Pradesh in public health service satisfaction with 81.6 percent, while Kurnool ranked last. The rankings were based on patient feedback collected via an automated voice system. Authorities have issued show-cause notices to 135 medical officers regarding the performance of local health centres.

stories.title: Anti-cancer drug prices capped
stories.summary: New price caps on 1,364 anti-cancer formulations took effect on November 9, 2026. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority estimates the move will save consumers ₹3,540 crore annually. The decision follows recommendations from an expert committee tasked with capping trade margins on 137 specific cancer drugs.

stories.title: Cervical cancer remains a global health challenge
stories.summary: Cervical cancer is largely preventable through HPV vaccination and screening, yet it remains the fifth most common cancer in women. Low- and middle-income countries face the highest mortality rates due to inequities in access to care. Persistent HPV infection is the primary cause of the disease.

stories.title: Measles cases surge in the U.S.
stories.summary: The United States is nearing the loss of its measles-free status as cases rise and childhood vaccination defenses weaken. The resurgence follows years of vaccine opposition. The full data investigation into the country's shifting immunization landscape is available for subscribers.

stories.title: Cholera deaths exceed 3,000
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reports that cholera has killed more than 3,000 people globally this year. Despite the rising death toll, the organization maintains that its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remains within reach.

stories.title: Experimental Ebola vaccines join Congo trial
stories.summary: Two experimental vaccines, Oxford’s ChAdOx1 BDBV and Moderna’s mRNA-1469, will join the Phase 2/3 Tumaini trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The trial aims to address the ongoing Bundibugyo virus outbreak, adding to the existing Ervebo vaccine currently in use.

stories.title: CDC recruits staff for Ebola screenings
stories.summary: The CDC has issued an urgent request for staff volunteers to screen passengers arriving from Central Africa for Ebola. The move follows the temporary barring of non-U.S. citizens who recently visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The agency is currently bolstering its airport presence.

stories.title: RFK Jr. claims cyclosporiasis outbreak is controlled
stories.summary: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. stated that the multi-state cyclosporiasis outbreak is under control. The parasitic illness has sickened at least 1,600 people across five states. Officials claim to have identified the source through epidemiological forensics.

stories.title: Salmonella Javiana outbreak reaches 65 cases
stories.summary: A Salmonella Javiana outbreak has grown to 65 reported illnesses across the U.S. The FDA is tracing the supply chain but has yet to identify a specific food source, brand, or manufacturer. The number of cases increased by six in the week leading up to November 4.

stories.title: Thailand monitors evolving Mpox symptoms
stories.summary: Thai health officials report that Clade Ib is now the primary Mpox strain. Patients are presenting with atypical symptoms like tonsillitis and buttock boils, complicating early diagnosis. Authorities are advising medical staff to look beyond classical skin eruptions to identify potential cases.

stories.title: Train collision in Egypt kills four
stories.summary: Two passenger trains collided 76 km south of Cairo on Sunday, killing at least four people and injuring 88. The state railway authority reported that a train travelling to Fayoum struck the rear of another heading to Aswan, causing several cars to derail.

stories.title: AI tools for medical reports
stories.summary: Researchers at the Universidad Carlos III de Madrid have evaluated AI models for simplifying medical reports. The study suggests these tools can help patients understand their health conditions, though the team notes that human oversight remains necessary to ensure accuracy.

stories.title: Google.org funds TB screening startup
stories.summary: Google.org has provided $2.3 million in funding and cloud credits to Pune-based Froncort.AI. The startup uses AI to guide frontline workers in identifying areas susceptible to tuberculosis. The investment is intended to triple screening efficiency and support the development of the company's mAI-NETRA platform.

stories.title: Ellipsis Health acquires Kouper Health
stories.summary: Voice AI startup Ellipsis Health has acquired Kouper Health for an undisclosed amount. The move aims to integrate technology that translates patient conversations into operational actions, such as scheduling and care coordination. The company plans to extend its voice AI capabilities beyond simple patient communication.

stories.title: Trauma linked to cardiovascular risk
stories.summary: Mental health conditions including PTSD, depression, and substance abuse following trauma are linked to a higher risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack, and stroke. This finding comes from new, independent research published in the Journal of the American Heart Association. Trauma is a common human experience.

stories.title: Maternal mental health chatbot trial results
stories.summary: A study of 400 maternal patients found that using a generative AI chatbot for mental health support was insufficient for improving anxiety or depression outcomes. Participants in the experimental group were offered $0.50 per quiz to sustain engagement. The control group received a children's book.

stories.title: Layered Crises Shape Adolescent Mental Health in Sierra Leone, Qualitative
stories.summary: Layered and intersecting crises shape adolescent mental health in Sierra Leone to an extent that exceeds individual-level coping strategies, according to findings from a qualitative participatory study. Young people across Sierra Leone have endured multiple major disruptions in recent decades, including civil conflict, the 2014

stories.title: Desire for legacy linked to mental health
stories.summary: A study of 2,912 Israeli adults published in the International Journal of Mental Health and Addiction found that people who believe they will be remembered after death report better mental health. These individuals also reported fewer symptoms of anxiety, depression, and substance abuse issues.

stories.title: Utah families donate $35 million for mental health research
stories.summary: The Huntsman Mental Health Foundation has received a $35 million gift from Gail Miller and the Larry H. Miller & Gail Miller Family Foundation. The investment will fund a research facility intended to accelerate the discovery and application of new treatments for mental health challenges.

stories.title: Forbes reviews online therapy platforms
stories.summary: Forbes has published a list of the 10 best online therapy platforms for 2026. The full article is currently unavailable to readers using ad blockers. The platform remains inaccessible to those who prefer not to disable their security software.

stories.title: Medical Xpress discusses paternal mental health
stories.summary: Medical Xpress has published a report regarding the state of paternal mental health. The full text of the article is currently blocked by a connection verification tool. The site is checking for automated abuse before allowing access to the content.

stories.title: Study links depression to lower employment in Indian adults
stories.summary: A study of 27,092 Indian adults aged 45 to 60 years found that increased depressive symptoms correlate with a lower likelihood of employment. Researchers used the Composite International Diagnostic Interview to assess participants. The findings suggest that mental health and workforce participation are clearly linked.

stories.title: Young people struggle with mental health survey questions
stories.summary: A qualitative study found that young people interpret standard mental health survey questions differently than intended. Researchers suggest that survey responses may reflect individual reasoning rather than actual mental health conditions. The investigation was prompted by contradictory trends in reported well-being and declining health among youth.

research.title: A novel candidate biomarker for detecting premalignant and early ovarian cancer
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 10 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04755-2 New data suggest that the long noncoding RNA known as Tu-Stroma represents a promising new circulating biomarker for the detection of ovarian cancer at premalignant and early stages, for which sensitive screening methods currently are lacking.

research.title: Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain
research.summary: A surprising discovery suggests that some early signs of Alzheimer’s disease may begin outside the brain. Using miniature laboratory systems made from human cells, scientists found that genetic mutations associated with inherited Alzheimer’s can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without any involvement from the brain or spinal cord. This could.

research.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 10 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04732-9 Tested in a cohort of 506 individuals, the RNA-based biomarker of microenvironment fitness Tu-stroma shows high performance in discriminating early-stage ovarian cancer from benign lesions, outperforming CA125.

research.title: Cancer uses antioxidants to disarm the immune system, scientists discover
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that tumors release natural antioxidants to shut down the immune cells responsible for destroying cancer, exploiting a surprising weakness in the body's defenses. Blocking this mechanism in mice restored immune activity and improved immunotherapy responses, potentially opening a new path toward more effective cancer treatments.

research.title: Next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor improves survival in lung cancer
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 10 November 2026, doi:10.1038/d41591-026-00057-9 Phase 3 trial data show that the next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor divarasib leads to longer progression-free survival than the first-generation inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib in patients with non, small-cell lung cancer.

research.title: Why heart attacks can still happen even when bad cholesterol is low
research.summary: Even when bad cholesterol is brought down to healthy levels, some people remain at risk of heart attacks, and scientists may have discovered why. Researchers identified two types of fat-carrying particles that appear to promote inflammation and damage blood vessels through mechanisms beyond cholesterol buildup.

research.title: A 24-hour fast triggers a surprising repair response in the gut
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that fasting for just 24 hours increases a beneficial gut bacterium that helps the intestines regenerate after radiation damage. The preclinical findings could pave the way for new treatments that protect healthy tissue during cancer therapy, potentially without requiring patients to fast.
